Monospace typography (Azeret Mono) paired with clean sans-serif (Matter) creates a technical-yet-refined editorial sensibility. Animated 3D carousel of UI mockups and Lottie illustrations add dimensionality to an otherwise flat, minimalist aesthetic.

fields.description: A private, hands-on evening for developers and design engineers who are tired of generic AI output. You'll bring an agent, a product or a half-built idea. You'll leave with it wired to the Taste Brand API, so every screen, email and asset your agent produces follows a real brand system instead of drifting toward average. There are no keynotes, only builders, working code and short demos. Concept draft only: the date, venue, capacity and budget are unverified assumptions, and registration is not open.
fields.audience: Developers, design engineers and technical founders in San Francisco who are building AI products and care about the quality and consistency of what their agents generate.
fields.format: In-person evening build session with a short orientation, two guided build blocks with Taste engineers on hand, and 3-minute demos. Invite-only, with a planning assumption of about 60–100 attendees (unverified).
fields.agenda:

0:00 Doors, check-in, API keys, light food
0:30 Orientation (10 min): why agents drift off-brand, plus a live Brand API walkthrough
0:45 Build block 1: wire the Brand API into your agent or starter repo
1:45 Break: food refresh, pairing swaps

fields.productionBrief:
STATUS: private, unpublished concept draft. Nothing has been booked, published, sent or spent.

CONFIRMED (brief:1): Company Taste Labs. Objective: adoption. Audience: developers and design engineers building AI products. Topics: Brand API, AI agents, design engineering. Geography: San Francisco first. Window: 2026-10-01 to 2026-11-30. Budget ceiling: USD 5,000. No sending, spending or public registration.

ASSUMPTIONS (all unverified):
- Date: a weekday evening in mid-to-late Oct or Nov 2026. Not fixed, so the date field is blank.
- Venue: an SF partner office or community space, still to be chosen and not booked. The location field is blank.
- Capacity: about 60–100.
- Budget: USD 5,000 is the total ceiling across this event AND any sponsorship. No costs have been quoted.
- Pricing: free for invitees is a proposal only. No ticket price has been decided.
- No speakers, partners, caterers or guests have been contacted or committed.

OPEN QUESTIONS: How should the budget split with sponsorship? Is an in-kind venue partner available? What API credit limits apply for attendees? How many Taste engineers will staff the event?

SOURCES: brief:1. The Taste brand extraction was used as visual reference only.

experience.venue: Selection criteria (nothing has been chosen or booked): a San Francisco loft or studio-style space, ideally in SoMa, Mission or Dogpatch, with a dimmable dark interior. It needs worktables and power for 60–100 people, Wi-Fi for 100+ devices, a demo screen wall, access until about 10pm, and permission for outside catering. Preferred: a partner office offered in kind. Fallback: a coworking or community event space. Avoid hotel or conference rooms.
experience.guests: Invite people who are actively shipping AI products with visible output, such as generated UI, assets, docs or content. Proposed mix: about 50% developers and AI engineers, 30% design engineers, and 20% technical founders and product leads. Screening question: 'What does your agent generate, and where does it go off-brand?' Favour people bringing real projects. Nobody has been contacted. Invite copy: 'Your agent can write, design and ship. It just doesn't sound like you. Bring a project, wire in the Taste Brand API, and demo the before and after. Invite-only. Date and venue to be announced.'
experience.atmosphere: Lighting: low ambient light near black, focused task light on the tables, and a single System Blue (#0000EE) wash on the demo wall. Sound: minimal instrumental or ambient music at conversation level during builds, silence for orientation and demos, and one handheld mic. Signage: Paper White type in Azeret Semimono on near-black boards. Photography: documentary style with no step-and-repeat. Shoot hands on keys, before/after screens, and faces lit by monitors, with high contrast and grain.
experience.artDirection: No brand imagery is available, so the cover is left empty. For a future commissioned image: a dark editorial frame (#111111/#1E1E1E) with one monitor lighting a worktable. On screen, a generic UI sits beside an on-brand version, with a thin System Blue accent. Set the title in Matter and the promise line in Azeret Semimono, in Paper White and Muted Gray. No stock crowds or robot imagery. Page: dark hero, cream agenda and guest sections, dark CTA with an outlined blue button, and a 'date and venue TBC' note.
experience.foodAndDrink: One-handed food suited to keyboards: family-style trays from a local SF taqueria or dumpling caterer at doors, and a smaller second drop at the break. Include vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options labelled on monospace cards. Sparkling water, cold brew and craft sodas throughout. Beer and natural wine only after demos, if the venue's licensing allows. Self-serve. No caterer has been contacted.
experience.budgetGuidance: Estimates only, nothing quoted. Ceiling: USD 5,000 total, shared with sponsorship. At about 80 guests: venue USD 0–1,500 (0 if a partner hosts in kind), food and soft drinks USD 1,600–2,200, beer and wine USD 300–500, AV and power USD 200–600, signage and badges USD 150–300, photographer USD 400–800, contingency about USD 300–450. Indicative total with an in-kind venue: USD 3,000–4,500, leaving about USD 500–2,000 for sponsorship. A paid venue would absorb that headroom. Attendee pricing is undecided.

design.enhancedPrompt:
Build Night: A private evening for developers and design engineers building AI products who want their AI agents to output on-brand designs by wiring a brand API directly into their workflows.

Audience: Design-conscious technologists frustrated by generic AI output who care about craft, precision, and maintaining creative standards at scale. They use this event to learn a technical skill (API integration) while solving a real problem (AI slop) in a focused, hands-on format.

Constraints: Single-page event microsite. Desktop-first but mobile-responsive (992px+ primary, 768px tablet, mobile stacks to 1 column). Dark-dominant layout with clean editorial structure. Not a conference page—this is a workshop for builders.

Visual Direction:

Background: Deep black (#1E1E1E) with sections alternating to off-white cream (#F5F7F2) only where necessary to create rhythm. Hero stays dark. Agenda and attendee sections on cream. CTA zone returns to dark.

Typography: 
- Page title (Hero): Matter, clamp(2rem, 3vw, 2.2rem), 400 weight, 1.2em line-height, color #F5F7F2
- Section headlines (What You'll Build, Agenda, Who Should Come): Matter, clamp(1.8rem, 2.2vw, 2rem), 400 weight, 1.25em line-height
- One-line promise: Azeret Semimono, clamp(1rem, 1.05vw, 1.1rem), 400 weight, 1.5em line-height, color #8B8B8B on dark sections
- Body copy: Matter, clamp(1rem, 1.05vw, 1.1rem), 300 weight, 1.5em line-height
- Date/venue disclaimer: Azeret Semimono, 12px, 500 weight, 1em line-height, color #8B8B8B
- Button text: Azeret Semimono, 15px, 400 weight

Layout: 12-column grid, 2rem gutter, 90rem max-width, centered symmetry. Hero full-bleed. Content sections constrained to 8 columns center (span 3-10). Generous vertical padding: 10rem between major sections on desktop, 4rem on mobile.

Colors:
- Dark sections: background #1E1E1E, headlines #F5F7F2, body #F5F7F2, secondary text #8B8B8B
- Light sections: background #F5F7F2, headlines #333333, body #333333
- Interactive blue (CTA button): #002BBA text on transparent background with 1px solid #002BBA border
- Dividers: #747370, 1px solid

Spacing: Section separation alternates background color (black → cream → black). Use 4rem–10rem vertical padding per section. Internal spacing uses grid gutter (2rem).

Buttons:
Request Invite CTA: Azeret Semimono 15px, padding 0.43rem 2rem, border-radius rounded, background transparent, border 1px solid #002BBA, text #002BBA. Hover: background #002BBA, text #F5F7F2.

Borders: Horizontal dividers in agenda list items use 1px solid #747370. No card borders—separation through whitespace and alternating backgrounds.

Structure:
1. Hero (dark #1E1E1E): Short title "Build Night" + one-line promise immediately below in Azeret Semimono gray
2. What You'll Build (cream #F5F7F2): 2-3 sentence paragraph explaining the API integration outcome
3. Agenda (cream #F5F7F2): Time-blocked list with stroke dividers (#747370), flush-left alignment
4. Who Should Come (cream #F5F7F2): 3-4 bullet points in clean list format
5. Request Invite CTA (dark #1E1E1E): Centered button with generous breathing room
6. Date/Venue Note (dark #1E1E1E): Small disclaimer in Azeret Semimono 12px, #8B8B8B, centered below CTA, clearly labeled "Note: Date and venue to be confirmed"

Shadows: None. Elevation through color contrast only.

Animations: Minimal. Button hover transitions at 0.2s ease. Underline on text links scales from 0 to 1 with GSAP cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0, 1). No carousels, no video, no Lottie—static editorial clarity.

Icons: If directional cues needed (e.g., arrow in button), use monoline SVG 1.4px stroke, 16px size, currentColor.

events.title: Beyond Generic Output
events.rationale: A live critique salon for AI builders. Bring an artifact, learn what makes it feel generic, then improve it with people who care about craft.

fields.title: Beyond Generic Output
fields.description: An evening of live critique for people who build with AI and refuse to ship average. Bring one piece of AI-generated work: a UI, a paragraph of copy, an image, a track. Practitioners with strong taste will take it apart on stage. They'll name exactly why it reads as generic, then show how taste-driven evaluation and quality infrastructure can push output past 'good enough' at scale. It's hands-on, intimate and deliberately opinionated. Hosted by Taste. Date, venue and pricing are still pending; everything on this page is a private proposal.
fields.audience: About 80–120 invited guests (working assumption): developers and design engineers building AI apps; AI/ML engineers and researchers working on subjective judgment, evaluation and taste; technical founders and product leaders at AI companies responsible for output quality; and design-conscious technologists frustrated by generic AI output.
fields.format: In-person evening salon: live critique, demos and hands-on stations
fields.agenda:
Proposed run-of-show (times relative to doors, date TBD):
+0:00 Doors. Submission check-in: guests confirm their pre-submitted artifact and receive a monospace 'specimen card'. Low ambient sound, drinks.
+0:30 Opening thesis, 10 min. Taste host: 'Generic is a default, not a destiny.'
+0:40 Live Critique Round 1, 35 min. Interface & Language: 6–8 submissions on the big screen, a 2–3 person critic panel, 4 min each. Verdict: what makes it generic, one concrete fix.
+1:15 Demo: Measuring taste, 15 min. How preference data and evaluation loops turn subjective judgment into a quality signal (speaker TBD).
+1:30 Intermission, 20 min. Food service, specimen wall browsing.
+1:50 Live Critique Round 2, 35 min. Image & Sound: 6–8 submissions, including one live before/after regeneration.
+2:25 Critique stations, 45 min. Four track tables with a practitioner at each; guests iterate on their own artifact with feedback.
+3:10 Closing: 'The Specimen Wall' reveal of the evening's strongest before/after pairs; next steps with Taste. 5 min.
+3:15–3:45 Late conversation, then close.
fields.host: Taste (tastelabs.com). Critics, demo speakers and station leads are proposed roles only; none are confirmed.
fields.cta: Request an invite. Include one AI-generated artifact you want critiqued and a sentence on what feels off about it. Space is curated; submitting doesn't guarantee a place or an on-stage critique.
fields.productionBrief:
PRIVATE, NONBINDING PROPOSAL. Nothing booked, sent, spent or published.
CONFIRMED (brief:1): Taste hosts; adoption goal; SF first; window Oct 1–Nov 30 2026; $15,000 USD cap.
ASSUMPTIONS: date TBD (Tue–Thu evening); SF venue unsourced; timezone is blank until confirmed; ~80–120 capacity; no costs quoted; no critics or speakers confirmed.
PRICE: PENDING. Not free or paid until decided.
OPEN: date, venue, price, critic panel, submission consent/moderation, photo consent, sponsor (Scout/Partnerships).
INVITE COPY: 'Bring the thing your model got almost right. Most AI output isn't wrong, just average. Taste is hosting a small evening of live critique in SF [date TBD]. Send one artifact; some go on the big screen. ~100 seats, by application.'
SOUND: low minimal electronic at doors/intermission; 2 handhelds + host lav; full-range PA check for audio critiques.
LIGHTING: dark room, projection brightest; warm key on critics; single #0000EE accent.
PHOTO: 1 photographer ~3.5h, documentary, screen-lit, consent opt-out lanyards.
RISKS: pre-screen submissions; pre-recorded demo fallback.

experience.venue: Character: raw, dark and editorial. Picture a gallery, warehouse or design studio in SoMa, Dogpatch or the Mission (proposals only; none sourced or booked). Criteria: ~100–150 standing / ~90 seated; a projection surface at least 3m wide with blackout; room for four station zones; PA and load-in access; controllable warm lighting; transit access; catering allowed; weekday evening availability Oct–Nov 2026; rental at or under ~$4,500.
experience.guests: ~80–120 (assumption), by application with a required artifact. Mix: ~35% developers & design engineers building AI apps; ~20% AI/ML eval and preference researchers; ~25% technical founders and product leads at AI companies; ~20% design-conscious technologists and creatives working with AI. Max ~3 per company; ~15% of seats held for critics, partners and Taste team. Critics and station leads to be identified later; no commitments.
experience.atmosphere: Intimate and exacting, like a design crit held in a darkroom. The room is near-black with cream type and a single System Blue accent, and the projected artifact is always the brightest thing in it. Sound stays low and minimal so conversation carries. The spirit is critique as respect: sharp verdicts, no dunking, and every note ends with a concrete fix. Signage and specimen cards are set in Azeret Semimono and Matter.
experience.artDirection: The cover uses an existing Taste brand image (the Design Philosophy Timeline card). Future commissioned hero: one artifact shown twice on #111111. The generic version sits left, flattened in gray #8B8B8B; the refined version sits right, crisp in #F5F7F2, joined by a thin #0000EE annotation line with mono margin notes. No stock photos or robots. Print: A6 cream specimen cards, a before/after specimen wall, minimal black signage. No commissioned or generated image exists yet.
experience.foodAndDrink: Proposal; no caterer sourced. A 'specimen' menu of 4–5 hand-held composed bites on black slate, each labeled in mono: seasonal crudo, charred vegetable skewer, mushroom tartine, vegan grain cup, dark chocolate and sea salt. At least 2 vegan and 2 gluten-free options. Bar: signature cocktail 'The Second Draft' plus a zero-proof twin, local natural wine, NA beer, sparkling water. Assume ~$45–60 per guest; confirm licensing.
experience.budgetGuidance: Planning ranges only; no quotes. At about 100 guests: venue $3,000–4,500; food and drink with staff $4,500–6,000; AV $1,500–2,200; lighting $300–600; photography $800–1,200; print $300–500; tooling $0–200; other staff and rentals $400–800; contingency $1,300–1,500. Total: $12,100–17,500. The upper estimate is $2,500 over the $15,000 cap. Reduce scope or obtain lower quotes before approval. No revenue or sponsor funding is assumed.

They're visiting this page because they received a direct invite or discovered it through Taste's network. The page serves as confirmation, atmosphere-setting, and RSVP collection.

Colors: Near-black background #1E1E1E. All typography in Paper White #F5F7F2. Single accent: System Blue #0000EE for the RSVP button only. No other colors. Strict high-contrast binary.

Typography: Event title 'Beyond Generic Output' in Azeret Semimono, clamp(2.5rem, 4vw, 4rem), font-weight 400, line-height 1.2em, color #F5F7F2. Subtitle 'A Taste-hosted critique evening for AI builders' in Matter, clamp(1.2rem, 1.6vw, 1.4rem), font-weight 400, line-height 1.25em, color #F5F7F2. Event details (Date/Venue/Price) in Matter, clamp(1rem, 1.05vw, 1.1rem), font-weight 300, line-height 1.5em, color #8B8B8B for labels, #F5F7F2 for values. Each detail shows label in Muted Gray #8B8B8B followed by 'Pending' in Paper White #F5F7F2. Body description text in Matter, clamp(1rem, 1.05vw, 1.1rem), font-weight 300, line-height 1.5em, color #F5F7F2.

Spacing: Section padding 4rem vertical on mobile, 6rem–8rem on desktop. Between title and subtitle: 1.5rem. Between subtitle and details block: 3rem. Between detail rows: 1rem. Between details block and description: 3rem. Between description and RSVP button: 3rem.

Shadows: None. Borders: 1px solid #FFFFFF0D (5% white) around detail block container if needed for structure. Otherwise no borders.

Button: RSVP button in System Blue #0000EE background, Paper White #F5F7F2 text, Azeret Semimono font, 15px size, 0.43rem vertical padding, 2rem horizontal padding, fully rounded corners. Hover: invert to Paper White #F5F7F2 background, Ink Black #333333 text. Transition: all 0.2s. Button centered horizontally.

Animations: Fade-in on page load (opacity 0 to 1 over 0.6s, matching tastePageIn keyframe). Hover transition on button (all 0.2s).

Layout structure: Centered vertical stack. Top: Event title (Azeret Semimono display). Below: Subtitle (Matter). Below: Detail block with three rows—'Date: Pending', 'Venue: Pending', 'Price: Pending'—each label in #8B8B8B, value in #F5F7F2, left-aligned within centered container. Below: 2–3 sentence description of the event purpose (critique AI outputs, discuss taste in AI systems, intimate gathering for SF builders). Below: RSVP button centered.

No navigation bar. No footer. No images. No icons. Pure typographic hierarchy on dark void. Emphasis on clarity, restraint, and intellectual seriousness matching Taste's Swiss Style editorial sensibility.

outreachDrafts.subject: Sponsorship inquiry: FLOCK – The Autonomous-Ops Summit (listed 2026-10-14, San Francisco)
outreachDrafts.body:
Hello FLOCK organizing team,

I'm writing on behalf of Taste Labs (tastelabs.com). We make infrastructure that helps AI products produce output that meets brand and design standards. Our audience is developers and design engineers building AI products, and our focus areas are our Brand API, AI agents and design engineering.

We saw FLOCK – The Autonomous-Ops Summit listed in a public conference directory for 2026-10-14 in San Francisco. We have not yet been able to confirm the details on your official site, so we'd appreciate some clarification before deciding whether a sponsorship would suit both sides. We understand the summit's main focus may be SRE and autonomous operations, so we're especially interested in how many attendees build AI products or agents.

To be upfront, our sponsorship budget for this period is limited and not yet decided. This message is only a request for information. It is not a commitment, and nothing is being agreed or purchased.

The questions are listed below. If there is a sponsorship prospectus or a better person to contact, we'd be grateful for a pointer.

Thank you for your time.

Best regards,
[Sender name and title – to be filled in by Taste Labs]
Taste Labs
questions: Is FLOCK confirmed to take place on 2026-10-14 in San Francisco? Is NeuBird AI the organizer?
What is the venue, and what are the start and end times (timezone)?
What is the format: in person, hybrid or virtual? Talks, workshops, expo, networking?
Roughly how are attendees split between AI product and agent builders, design engineers, and SRE/ops engineers?
Do you offer sponsorships for this event, and is there space available?
What sponsorship tiers are available, what does each include, and what does each cost (with any additional fees)?
Is there a sponsorship prospectus, a deadline for committing, or a specific contact for sponsorship?
